text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired -> service: metering-usage-high-watermark. Priority: P1. Symptom: usage ingestion backlog > 30m, writes to billing ledger delayed, potential invoice risk. PD link: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Trigger: metering-ingest-backpressure-rule; escalation policy: metering-oncall -> oncall-primary -> oncall-sre.

Erin (oncall): acked the page. I'm on it. Starting triage — pinging data-ops + billing.

Lee (data-ops): seeing a steady spike in kafka consumer lag on topic `usage.events.v2`. Consumer group `metering-ingest-consumers` lag ~ 2.3M messages, oldest offset ~ 00:14:21 ago.

Jon (billing): thanks. any evidence of token-count mismatch yet? customers have asked about delayed invoices.

Lee (data-ops): running quick counts:
```
-- clickhouse-ish pseudo SQL
SELECT count(*) FROM usage_events_v2 WHERE ingested_at > now() - interval 1 hour;
-- result: 18,200 (expected ~ 200k)
```
Backpressure looks real. DLQ rate has increased.

Ash (sre): what does the cluster look like? CPU/GPU not relevant but consumer pods/replicas?

Erin (oncall): jog through runbook: 1) identify producer surge or broker issue 2) ensure consumers not OOM/crashing 3) scale consumers or add temporary burst workers 4) enable de-dup/skip path for invoice-critical tokens 5) postmortem ticket.

Lee (data-ops): consumer pods are healthy but stalling on heavy message batches. Found repeated `TimeoutError` in logs when writing to `ingest-writer` (internal HTTP 504 from write-proxy). Pasting snippet: `2026-03-14T16:03:12Z ERROR writer write timeout for batch_id=abcd1234 status=504`.

Erin (oncall): ok that points to write-proxy saturation. Ash, can you check write-proxy autoscaling and connection pool metrics?

Ash (sre): looking. write-proxy CPU 95% on two nodes. Connection pool exhausted (max_fds ~ 4096 reached). Autoscaler didn't kick; we have a cooldown bug hit by transient API. Increasing replicas manually to 5 -> scaling initiated.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation notification sent to oncall-sre.

Sam (CS): customer impact: CS queue has 3 inbound enterprise tickets citing missing usage for yesterday -> potential invoice mismatch tomorrow. Need ETA for mitigation. Customers: Acme Corp, BrightSide.

Erin (oncall): Mitigation plan (short):
- manual upscale of write-proxy (Ash) -> +3 replicas (in progress)
- enable temporary bypass for invoice-critical route to `write-proxy-hot` which has staggered capacity (Lee)
- run partial catch-up workers (Lee) to drain hot partitions
- notify CS + customers with preliminary ETA (Maya/Sam)

Lee (data-ops): starting `catchup-consumer --partitions=keyed-invoices --rate=high` now. Expect initial drain of ~120k msg/hr for critical partitions.

Ash (sre): replicas up to 5, connection pool freed, error rate for writer dropping from 23% -> 4% in last 60s. Continuing to monitor.

Jon (billing): we should lock invoice window: set `invoice-run` to read-only for today if backlog not fully drained in 2h. Also creating temporary invoice-hold flag so billing jobs skip generation to avoid partial invoices.

Maya (product): flagging potential customer SL impact. If we hold invoices, we need a comms plan. Sam, prepare a short note: "We are experiencing ingestion backpressure affecting usage records; we expect resolution within 3 hours; billing run may be delayed. We're prioritizing invoice-critical records."

Sam (CS): drafting. Will send to Acme + BrightSide in 30m and post banner on status.redwood.ai.

Erin (oncall): status update: scaling + catch-up in progress, consumer lag for critical partitions down from 2.3M -> 1.1M in 15m. End-to-end ingestion latency improved from 42m -> 9m for hot partitions.

Lee (data-ops): starting targeted dedupe for replays to avoid token inflation. Running lightweight check: `hash(payload->customer_id, event_id)` against recent 24h index.

Erin (oncall): any sign this was caused by producer spike?

Lee (data-ops): preliminary: producer rate from integrations is normal. Root cause looks like write-proxy thread/connection leak + autoscaler cooldown prevented reactive scale. Will open infra bug.

Ash (sre): created ticket INFRA-4873: "write-proxy autoscaler cooldown missed sustained load -> connection pool exhaustion". Assigning to infra team.

pagerduty-bot: note: incident acknowledged by Erin. Next escalation window in 18m if unresolved.

Jon (billing): running a sanity check on token counts before we un-block invoices: `SELECT customer_id, count_distinct(token_id) FROM usage_ledger WHERE day = '2026-03-14' GROUP BY customer_id LIMIT 5;` sample shows counts behind expected by ~0.2% — likely caught by catch-up. I'll hold invoice run until final confirm.

Erin (oncall): temporary mitigation successful so far. Action items:
- Lee: finish catch-up + dedupe (ETA 90m)
- Ash: monitor autoscaler fix + link to INFRA-4873 (ETA followup in 24h)
- Jon: keep invoice hold flag and re-check counts post-drain (ETA 2h)
- Sam/Maya: customer comms sent and status page updated (in progress)

Maya (product): please add to next Monday weekly: postmortem + RCA + runbook update for autoscaler.

Sam (CS): sent emails to affected customers with placeholder ETA.

Erin (oncall): final note for now: incident severity remains P1 until invoice run/unblocked. Keeping thread open. If anybody needs to join war room, call +1-555-1234. :phone:

-- end of thread --
